findings.summary: The trailing `flush()` after the loop is called without `await` (unlike the in-loop `await flush()` at line 244). `embedAll` executes `return vectors;` immediately while the last batch's `embedBatch` network call is still in flight, so the returned `vectors` array is missing the final batch's embeddings whenever `batch` isn't already empty when the loop ends — i.e. on essentially every real ingestion. Downstream, `vectorizeUpsert` builds records as `chunks.map((_, i) => ({..., values: vectors[i], ...}))` (lines 424-428), so the tail chunks get `values: undefined` written to Vectorize — after the old vectors for that document were already deleted (line 407). This directly violates the brief's requirement that 'any partial batch at the end still gets sent' and corrupts the index for every document ingested.

findings.summary: The implementer's report claims tests were written and run for this change, but `git show --stat` on the commit shows only scripts/ingest.ts changed (1 file) — no test file was added or modified, and nothing in the existing vitest suite exercises embedAll. A test asserting `(await embedAll(...)).length === texts.length` would have caught the missing-await bug above.
